note: Adapted from the revision of Sands (1965), originally in English; the original describes the alate, soldier and worker, but the IA full text is a single text stream and the later part of this species (soldier, worker, measurements) is heavily interleaved with other entries in the OCR, so only the legible alate description is included here; measurements are not recorded.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule, middle of the frons and vertex brown to dark chestnut brown; vertex with 3 branching yellowish brown longitudinal stripes; postclypeus and the periocular region yellowish brown, that region extending backwards behind the eye to a point and forwards to the base of the mandibles; labrum and antennae yellow to yellowish brown. Pronotum yellow to yellowish brown; mesonotum and metanotum, the other thoracic sclerites and the legs yellow. Abdominal tergites brown to dark chestnut brown, slightly darker around the spiracles, with yellow to yellowish brown margins, the anterolateral corners slightly paler; sternites yellow to yellowish brown, brown around the spiracles. Wings translucent pale brown, the subcosta and radial sector yellow, becoming paler towards the apex, the latter with a brown outline at the base, the membrane between them with a short brown section from the wing suture; the membrane behind the radial sector with or without orange yellow longitudinal streaks; the remaining veins fine yellowish brown to brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule much less than a semicircle behind the eyes, slightly undulate immediately behind the eyes; fontanelle distinct, usually Y-shaped, the lateral arms slightly swollen at the apex.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands treated Eutermes mobilis Sjöstedt, 1904, Eutermes tchadensis Sjöstedt, 1911 and Eutermes schubotzianus Sjöstedt, 1914 all as new synonyms of this species; the alate can be distinguished from similar species by the posterior margin of the head, the shape of the fontanelle and the body colour.
